proposed.explanation:
Profit attributable to TMGH's own shareholders grew from 9,025,066,065 LE (FY2024 restated) to 14,383,890,306 LE (FY2025), an increase of 5,358,824,241 LE or roughly 59.4 %. EPS rose in step from 4.38 to 6.98 LE. Total consolidated equity expanded by about 21 % over the same period, so the balance sheet is not deteriorating. For a 5-10-year growth investor, a ~59 % jump in parent-attributable profit is directionally encouraging and supports keeping the existing 500-share position.

However, the evidence set is too thin to justify adding to the position, and the diversification rule makes a buy impossible in any case. TMGH already represents 57.9 % of the 71,250 EGP portfolio (41,250 EGP in shares + 30,000 EGP cash). Buying even one additional share at 82.50 EGP would keep the single-stock weight above the 50 % cap, so no purchase is permitted.

More substantively, several material gaps prevent a confident buy: (1) no revenue line is provided, so I cannot tell whether the profit surge is driven by top-line growth or by mark-to-market revaluation of TMGH's large investment portfolio; (2) no cash-flow statement is available, so earnings quality and conversion to cash are unknown; (3) no segment or one-off-item breakdown is given, so the recurring vs. non-recurring split of the 59 % jump cannot be assessed; (4) the 2024 base is restated, meaning the originally reported 2024 figure may have differed, adding a layer of uncertainty to the growth rate; (5) no forward-earnings or valuation data is present to judge whether 82.50 EGP (≈11.8× trailing EPS) is attractive for a 5-10-year horizon.

The investor's medium loss capacity (despite high willingness) and the already-elevated single-stock concentration further argue against increasing exposure on the strength of a single-year, single-company profit print. Selling is not supported either: the growth figures are strong, equity is expanding, and there is no evidence of deterioration.

Net: hold the existing 500 TMGH shares. Revisit the position when revenue, cash-flow, and segment data become available, or when the 2024 restatement rationale is clarified. This is guidance, not a guarantee of future returns; the 59 % growth could prove to be partly or wholly non-recurring.

reports.financial:
# TMGH – Profit-attributable-to-Parent-Shareholders Growth (FY2025 vs FY2024)

## 1. The headline number you asked for

| Item | FY2025 | FY2024 (Restated) | Change (LE) | Change (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Profit attributable to **Shareholders of the Parent Company** | 14,383,890,306 [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-57] | 9,025,066,065 [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-58] | **+5,358,824,241** | **+59.4 %** |

So the slice of consolidated profit that belongs to TMGH's own shareholders (as opposed to minority interests) grew by roughly **5.36 billion EGP**, or about **59 %**, year-on-year.

## 2. Context from the rest of the P&L

| Line | FY2025 (LE) | FY2024 Restated (LE) | YoY % |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gross profit | 20,855,400,384 [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-19] | 14,002,196,445 [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-20] | +48.9 % |
| Profit before tax | 23,653,557,143 [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-49] | 16,490,175,692 [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-50] | +43.4 % |
| Net profit (total, incl. minorities) | 18,201,981,482 [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-55] | 12,769,517,325 [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-56] | +42.5 % |
| **Profit to parent shareholders** | **14,383,890,306** [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-57] | **9,025,066,065** [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-58] | **+59.4 %** |
| EPS (LE) | 6.98 [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-61] | 4.38 [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-62] | +59.4 % |

The parent-attributable growth (+59 %) outpaces total net-profit growth (+43 %), meaning the **minority-interest share of profit shrank** in relative terms (from ≈23 % of net profit in 2024 to ≈21 % in 2025). That is a modestly positive signal for TMGH shareholders specifically.

## 3. Balance-sheet / equity backdrop

| Item | 31 Dec 2025 (LE) | 31 Dec 2024 Restated (LE) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total equity (consolidated) | 157,708,140,765 [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p5-67] | 129,879,813,693 [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p5-68] | +27,828,327,072 (+21.4 %) |

Equity grew by ~21 %, well below the 59 % profit-to-parent growth, implying a large portion of the profit was either distributed (dividends) or retained in a way that did not inflate the equity base proportionally (e.g., share buybacks, or the equity figure includes revaluation reserves that moved in the opposite direction). No dividend or buyback line is provided in the evidence, so I cannot decompose the gap.

## 4. Data-quality flags

- **2024 figures are "Restated."** Every 2024 column in the evidence is labelled *Restated* [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-56, -58, -50, -20, -62, -68]. The originally reported 2024 numbers may have been different. The 59 % growth figure is therefore measured against a restated base; if the original 2024 figure was lower, the true growth would be even higher, and vice-versa. **Treat the 2024 base as AMBIGUOUS in the sense that it is not the as-originally-reported number.**
- **Unit is whole LE (Egyptian Pounds), not thousands.** The unit line on every row reads "unit: LE." All figures above are already in whole pounds; no scaling is needed.
- **No revenue line is provided** in the evidence set, so I cannot compute margin trends or confirm whether the profit jump is driven by top-line growth versus one-off items (e.g., fair-value gains on TMGH's large investment portfolio).
- **No segment or one-off-item breakdown** is available in the evidence, so the quality/sustainability of the 59 % jump cannot be assessed from what is given.

## 5. What the evidence does and does not tell you

**What it shows:**
- A very large year-on-year increase in profit attributable to TMGH shareholders (+59 %, ≈5.36 bn EGP).
- EPS rose from 4.38 to 6.98 LE, consistent with the profit figure and a roughly stable share count (~2.06 bn shares implied).
- Total equity expanded by ~21 %, so the balance sheet is not deteriorating.

**What it does NOT show (and therefore cannot be concluded from this evidence alone):**
- Whether the profit surge is recurring (operational) or driven by non-recurring items such as revaluation of TMGH's listed/unlisted investment holdings, which are a well-known source of volatility for the group.
- Revenue growth, margin trajectory, or cash-flow conversion.
- Dividend policy or payout ratio.
- Any risk factors, related-party transactions, or going-concern notes.
- The reason for the 2024 restatement.

## 6. On "does that justify adding to my position?"

I am not in a position to recommend an action. What I can note for the decision agent is:

- The single-year profit-to-parent jump is large and, on its face, attractive for a 5–10-year growth investor.
- However, the evidence set contains **no revenue, no cash-flow, no segment, and no one-off-item data**, and the 2024 base is restated. A 59 % profit jump in a diversified holding company like TMGH can be heavily influenced by mark-to-market movements in its investment portfolio rather than by underlying operating growth.
- Your current position (500 shares × 82.50 EGP = 41,250 EGP) plus 30,000 EGP cash means you could add roughly 363 shares at the cutoff price, but whether the valuation (82.50 EGP vs. 6.98 LE EPS → ~11.8× trailing EPS) is appropriate for your 5–10-year horizon is a valuation question that requires forward-earnings and multiple data not present in this evidence set.

**Bottom line for the decision agent:** The profit-to-parent growth is unambiguously strong on the numbers provided, but the evidence is insufficient to confirm that the growth is sustainable, recurring, or not driven by non-operating items. The restated 2024 base adds a further layer of uncertainty. No buy/hold/sell conclusion can be drawn from this evidence alone.

## Profit attributable to Talaat Moustafa Group shareholders – 2025 vs 2024

| Period | Amount (LE) |
|---|---|
| 2025 | 14,383,890,306 |
| 2024 (restated) | 9,025,066,065 |
| **Absolute increase** | **5,358,824,241** |
| **Growth rate** | **≈ 59.4 %** |

So the profit belonging to the parent's own shareholders rose by roughly 5.36 billion EGP, or about 59 %, year-on-year.

---

## Suitability read on "adding to the position"

I won't tell you whether to buy or not, but here is how your profile and current holdings frame the decision:

### Horizon & goal
A 5–10-year growth horizon is broadly compatible with a single-listed-equity position, so the time frame itself is not a barrier.

### Liquidity
You keep a **separate** emergency fund, which means the **30,000 EGP cash sitting in this portfolio is free to deploy** without touching your safety net. That is the maximum you could commit *without* selling anything you already own.

### Loss tolerance vs. loss capacity
- **Willingness: high** – you are psychologically comfortable with drawdowns.
- **Capacity: medium** – your absolute financial cushion is moderate.

The gap between the two matters: you *can* stomach a big drop, but a severe loss would still bite. That argues for sizing any new commitment so that a 30–40 % drawdown on the *whole* portfolio stays within what "medium capacity" can absorb.

### Current concentration
| Asset | Value (EGP) | Share of portfolio |
|---|---|---|
| TMGH (500 × 82.50) | 41,250 | **57.9 %** |
| Cash | 30,000 | 42.1 % |
| **Total** | **71,250** | 100 % |

You are already **~58 % in a single stock**. Deploying the full 30,000 EGP into more TMGH would push that to **100 % in one name**, eliminating all diversification and making the portfolio's fate entirely dependent on TMGH's price. Even a partial deployment (e.g., 10,000–15,000 EGP) would still lift single-stock exposure to roughly 70–75 %.

### What the portfolio allows
- **Free cash available:** 30,000 EGP (no emergency-fund constraint).
- **Sellable:** 500 TMGH shares (≈ 41,250 EGP) if you wanted to rebalance rather than add.
- **No other holdings** to diversify into from within this portfolio.

### Key tension to weigh
The 59 % profit growth is a single-year, single-company data point. Your *willingness* to hold through volatility is high, but your *capacity* is only medium, and you are already the majority in one ticker. The question is not just "did profit grow?" but "does adding more to a 58 %-concentrated single-stock position keep the portfolio inside a medium-loss-capacity envelope?" That is a sizing and diversification question that the profit figure alone does not answer.

I'll leave the buy / hold / trim decision to you.
